methodological_rigor.justification: The study integrates a notably broad toolkit: laser-capture microdissection with high-sensitivity mass spectrometry, noncontact coculture systems, 3D DRG coculture, sciatic nerve injection mouse models, AAV9-mediated neuronal RIPK1 KO, untargeted metabolomics, ELISA, Co-IP with point mutant validation, and SynergyFinder synergy analysis. Key mechanistic claims are validated with multiple orthogonal approaches (genetic KO + pharmacological inhibition + point mutants). Statistical analysis uses appropriate tests (ANOVA/Tukey, unpaired t-test, Kaplan-Meier/log-rank, multivariate Cox regression) with explicit normality testing (Shapiro-Wilk) and multiplicity correction (Tukey). Group sizes in the in vivo sciatic nerve model are stated (n=10 per group). One limitation is that the clinical patient cohort (n=66) is modest, and patient sample sizes for IHC/IF subanalyses vary (n=11-39 per group), limiting statistical power for clinical correlation analyses.

clinical_relevance_loe.justification: This preclinical mechanistic study addresses perineural invasion in gallbladder cancer, an aggressive malignancy with PNI in 71-96% of cases and independent prognostic significance demonstrated in this cohort (OR 2.36-7.03, P<0.001). The study provides direct clinical correlations with a 66-patient cohort using Kaplan-Meier and multivariate Cox regression. The identification of FPS-ZM1 (RAGE inhibitor) as synergistic with gemcitabine offers a clinically actionable combination strategy, and OGA expression in neural regions as a prognostic biomarker has direct translational utility. Clinical translation is limited by absence of prospective studies, small cohort size, and reliance on severely immunodeficient nude mouse models for in vivo efficacy.

reporting_quality.justification: Animal ethics approval is stated, and mouse strain, age, and source are specified. In vivo group sizes (n=10) are reported in figure legends. Statistical parameters are detailed in both the methods section and figure legends. However, reporting is incomplete in several areas: the clinical patient enrollment period (2013-2021, Xinhua Hospital) is stated but inclusion/exclusion criteria and consent procedures are only briefly mentioned; blinding of histopathological assessors is not described; sequencing data accession numbers are not provided in the main text; and the compound library used for screening is referenced only by the screening methodology rather than a specific catalog or repository. The methods section is comprehensive but densely formatted.

novelty_literature.justification: The demonstration that GBC-derived EVs transfer OGA protein to neurons, and that this transferred OGA deglycosylates RIPK1 at Ser440 specifically (switching it from O-GlcNAcylated/inhibited to phosphorylated/active) to trigger necroptosis represents a mechanistically novel EV-mediated tumor-nerve communication pathway. The identification of Ser440 as the critical competing glycosylation site antagonizing S166 phosphorylation, and the characterization of HMGB1-RAGE as the downstream effector loop completing the pro-invasion feedback, are novel contributions. Prior work had implicated EVs in PNI (pancreatic cancer lncRNAs, CAF-derived PIAT) but the OGA-RIPK1 necroptosis mechanism in GBC is distinct and mechanistically detailed.

writing_presentation.justification: The manuscript follows a clear logical structure from clinical observation through mechanistic dissection to therapeutic validation. The abstract concisely summarizes the key pathway. Figure legends are detailed and include quantitative descriptions. However, the results section is dense with consecutive mechanistic findings that occasionally lack clear transitional summary sentences, and the discussion is somewhat formulaic. Minor inconsistencies in figure numbering notation (e.g., 'Figure 1..' with double periods) suggest editorial formatting artifacts. The therapeutic validation in the final results section is well-integrated with the mechanistic story.

key_strengths: Identification of EV-mediated OGA transfer as a novel tumor-to-neuron communication mechanism, with mechanistic validation at multiple nodes including metabolomics, Co-IP, point mutants, and in vivo AAV9-RIPK1 KO

Pinpointing Ser440 as the critical O-GlcNAcylation site on RIPK1 that antagonizes S166 phosphorylation, supported by differential binding, glycosylation, and necroptosis phenotypes across four RIPK1 variants

Clinically grounded study with 66-patient GBC cohort demonstrating PNI-associated OGA upregulation and independent prognostic significance, combined with a therapeutically actionable FPS-ZM1/gemcitabine synergy finding
key_concerns: Clinical cohort is modest (n=66) and single-institution with no independent validation cohort; multivariate Cox regression includes PNI as a covariate but the absolute number of events is not stated

All in vivo tumor models use nude mice (BALB/c nude), precluding assessment of immune microenvironment contributions to PNI; the necroptosis-HMGB1-RAGE axis likely interacts with innate immune responses not captured in this model

The direct biochemical interaction between OGA and RIPK1 is supported by docking and co-IP but direct enzymatic deglycosylation of RIPK1 Ser440 by OGA is inferred rather than demonstrated with purified proteins; recombinant enzyme assays are acknowledged as future work in the discussion
chief_reviewer.rationale: This mechanistically detailed study reveals a novel EV-OGA-RIPK1 necroptosis-HMGB1-RAGE axis driving GBC perineural invasion with multi-level experimental validation and direct clinical correlates. The work is suitable for a mid-to-high tier cancer or gastroenterology journal (Tier 2) with minor revisions to improve clinical cohort reporting and clarify the biochemical validation of OGA-RIPK1 direct interaction.
